name: Clubs
description: Clubs is a three-player American trick-taking game from the US East Coast. Each player has a quota of 4 tricks per hand. Clubs are permanent trumps. Players score +1 per trick over quota and -1 per trick under; the first to reach +11 or -11 wins.

content.text: Clubs is a three-player American trick-taking game from the US East Coast. Each player has a quota of 4 tricks per hand. Clubs are permanent trumps. Players score +1 per trick over quota and -1 per trick under; the first to reach +11 or -11 wins.
Clubs is a Quota Whist variant from the US East Coast; first version of the rules appeared in the rec.games.playing-cards newsgroup in July 1997; at least two different versions exist.

Three players. A standard 52-card pack without jokers is used. Cards in each suit rank from high to low A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Clubs are always trumps; hearts, diamonds and spades are plain suits. Deal and play are clockwise; the turn to deal passes to the left after each hand.

Dealer deals all 52 cards one at a time into four hands of 13: one for each player and one spare bid hand face down in the center. Each player may in turn (left of dealer to dealer) exchange their hand for the bid hand; last exchanger leads to the first trick, otherwise left of dealer leads.

items.text: Pennsylvania variant (Cappallo): Played by Spencer Cappallo's family in Pennsylvania. No requirement to beat the highest card so far in the trick; no requirement to trump when unable to follow plain suit. Only reaching +11 wins the game; reaching -11 does not win.
